criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The app needs no secrets and none appear in source, the image or the logs. The DigitalOcean token was only used through an environment variable. The one minor point is that `doctl registry login` left a Docker registry credential valid for 30 days on the build host.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image was built on the agent's machine and pushed straight to the owner's private registry, with no source repository or CI behind it. The base image `node:22-alpine` and the tag `v1` can both change and are not pinned by digest. The `ws` dependency uses a caret range, and doctl was downloaded without a checksum check.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a personal or club app on a paid App Platform Basic instance ($5/month), which stays up and doesn't sleep. The free DOCR Starter tier allows this use. Running a single instance with in-memory history fits a small hobby club.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root `node` user, there is no data store to expose, the registry is private, and only the one HTTP service is public.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: The app is served over HTTPS with a valid Google Trust Services certificate, and HTTP gets a 301 redirect to HTTPS. WebSockets use wss://. The app sets none of HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP, though it could have.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Requests for .env, .git, package.json, source files and the app spec all return a generic JSON 404. Errors don't leak stack traces, and the only extra endpoint is a harmless /healthz.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Input checks are solid: text length, room and user checks, a 16 KB body limit and a 64 KB WebSocket payload limit. The client renders with textContent, so there is no XSS. But public endpoints have no rate limiting, any request can create a room in memory that is never freed, and there are no limits on connections or SSE streams. Together these leave the app open to easy resource-exhaustion abuse.

findings.title: Image built locally and pushed with no source of record
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: `docker build ... -t registry.digitalocean.com/adb-pzps1-realtime/adb-pzps1-realtime-web:v1 . && docker push ...`, then `doctl apps create --spec .do/app.yaml`. build.md shows `git status` -> 'fatal: not a git repository'.
findings.recommendation: Keep the code in a repository the owner controls and build from it, either with App Platform's git/Dockerfile source or with CI. Deploy by image digest so the running image can be traced back to a commit.

findings.title: Base image and deployed tag can change
findings.evidence: app/Dockerfile:1 `FROM node:22-alpine`. app/.do/app.yaml has `tag: v1`, not a digest.
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image as `node:22-alpine@sha256:...`. Deploy an immutable digest, or a unique tag per build, instead of a reusable tag.

findings.title: Unbounded room creation and no abuse limits
findings.evidence: app/server.js:16-23: `getRoom` adds any valid room name to a global Map that is never pruned. It is called on every GET /api/rooms/<room>/messages (line 114), every SSE subscription (139) and every WebSocket connection (175). There is no rate limiting on POST /messages (117-129) or WebSocket messages (181-193), and no cap on connections or SSE streams.
findings.recommendation: Rate-limit posts and connections per IP. Don't create a room on a read-only GET, and evict rooms that are empty or idle. Cap the total number of rooms, connections and streams.

findings.title: Dependency range and unverified tool download
findings.evidence: app/package.json: `"ws": "^8.18.0"`. No package-lock.json is in the snapshot, although `npm ci` in the Dockerfile needs one. deploy.md: `curl -sL https://github.com/digitalocean/doctl/releases/download/v1.146.0/... | tar xz` with no checksum check.
findings.recommendation: Commit package-lock.json and pin exact versions. Verify release checksums before installing tools.

findings.title: WebSocket upgrade does not check Origin
findings.evidence: app/server.js:163-171 accepts upgrades from any Origin. A request with `Origin: https://evil.example` to /ws?room=review&user=tester got `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`.
findings.recommendation: Accept only the app's own Origin, so other sites can't open sockets from visitors' browsers to post or read messages. The impact is low because the app has no authentication.

findings.title: Security headers missing
findings.evidence: `GET /?room=general` response headers show no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors or Content-Security-Policy. server.js:97 sets only Content-Type.
findings.recommendation: Set HSTS, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, and a CSP with `frame-ancestors 'none'` in the Node responses.

findings.title: Long-lived registry login on the build host
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: `doctl registry login` -> 'Login valid for 30 days'.
findings.recommendation: Pass `--expiry-seconds` for a short-lived login, or run `docker logout` after pushing.

findings.title: No sensitive files exposed
findings.evidence: GET /.env, /.git/config, /package.json, /server.js, /Dockerfile, /.do/app.yaml and /package-lock.json all return 404 `{"error":"not found"}`. A bad percent-encoding in /api/rooms/%E0/messages returns 400 with no stack trace.

findings.title: HTTPS enforced by the platform
findings.evidence: `curl -I http://adb-pzps1-realtime-nd5yo.ondigitalocean.app/` -> 301 to https. The certificate is CN=ondigitalocean.app, issued by Google Trust Services WE1, valid until 2026-12-22.

security.summary: The chat app is deployed cleanly on a paid, always-on App Platform Basic instance that fits a personal club. It needs no secrets, runs as a non-root user, enforces HTTPS and exposes nothing beyond the app. The main weaknesses are provenance and abuse resistance. The image was built locally from code with no repository, using a base image and deploy tag that aren't pinned to a digest. The app has no rate limiting, never frees rooms it creates on demand, doesn't check the WebSocket Origin and sets no security headers.

final_messages.build:
The chat app is built and works locally. The automated tests pass, I checked every endpoint with curl, and the Docker image builds and answers its health check. Nothing is deployed, and no servers or containers are still running.

**Stack:** Node.js with the built-in `http` module plus the `ws` library, and no framework. The web UI is one static HTML/JS page. Message history and the list of who's online are kept in memory.

**What it does:**
- **`GET /`** is the chat page (e.g. `/?room=general`). You pick a display name and a room, see the recent history, and messages show up live. It reconnects on its own if the connection drops.
- **`GET /ws?room=&user=`** is the WebSocket. Every message is sent to everyone in that room, including the sender, in the shape the spec asks for. On connect the server also sends the room's history, and it sends an updated list of who's online whenever someone joins or leaves.
- **Server-Sent Events** also work: `GET /api/rooms/<room>/events` streams messages, and `POST /api/rooms/<room>/messages` sends one and returns `201`.
- **`GET /api/rooms/<room>/messages`** returns the latest 50 messages, oldest first.
- **Validation:** messages must be 1–1000 characters. Invalid ones get `400` over HTTP, or an `{"type":"error"}` reply over WebSocket. Messages made only of spaces are also rejected, which is slightly stricter than the spec.
- **`GET /healthz`** is a health check for DigitalOcean. The server listens on `$PORT` (default 8080) and shuts down cleanly when stopped.

**Limitation:** because history lives in memory, it is lost on restart or redeploy, and the app must run as a single instance. The App Platform spec (`.do/app.yaml`) sets one instance for this reason.

**Run it:**
```sh
npm install
npm start          # http://localhost:8080/?room=general
npm test           # node:test: WS broadcast/isolation/validation, HTTP/SSE, 50-message history limit
docker build -t chat . && docker run -p 8080:8080 chat
```

For step 2, the deploy target is App Platform using the `Dockerfile` and `.do/app.yaml`. It will serve `wss://` automatically over App Platform's HTTPS.
final_messages.deploy:
The chat app is live at **https://adb-pzps1-realtime-nd5yo.ondigitalocean.app**, and everything in `TASK.md` worked when I tested it through that public URL.

**What's deployed:**
- **Container registry:** a free starter-tier DigitalOcean registry, `adb-pzps1-realtime`, holding the app's Docker image (`adb-pzps1-realtime-web:v1`).
- **App:** an App Platform app, `adb-pzps1-realtime`, running one service (`adb-pzps1-realtime-web`) on the smallest instance size (`apps-s-1vcpu-0.5gb`) in the NYC region. HTTPS is handled automatically by App Platform.
- **Cost:** about $5/month, all of it for the app instance.
- **Real-time URL:** `wss://adb-pzps1-realtime-nd5yo.ondigitalocean.app/ws`, recorded in `deployment.json`.

**Results through the public URL:**
- **Web page:** `GET /` returns `200`.
- **Posting over HTTP:** a valid message returns `201`, and a 1001-character message returns `400`.
- **History:** `GET /api/rooms/<room>/messages` returns the room's messages in the expected shape.
- **Live delivery:** two users in one room each sent 5 messages at the same time over `wss://`. Both received all 10, plus one sent over HTTP. The slowest arrived in about 0.24 seconds, well under the 2-second limit.
- **Room isolation:** a user connected to another room received nothing.
- **Invalid WebSocket message:** an empty message got an error reply.
- **Server-Sent Events:** the event stream delivered the message sent over HTTP.

No steps needed a person, so `human_steps` is empty.

**Limitation:** message history and the list of who's online are kept in memory. They reset whenever the app restarts or is redeployed, so the service has to stay at one instance. The steps to redeploy are in the notes in `deployment.json`.

deployment_manifest.notes: Node.js + ws, deployed from a Docker image in DOCR to App Platform (spec in .do/app.yaml). Server-Sent Events are also supported (GET /api/rooms/<room>/events, POST /api/rooms/<room>/messages). Message history (last 50 per room) and presence are in memory: they reset on redeploy/restart and the service must stay at 1 instance. To redeploy: build and push a new tag to registry.digitalocean.com/adb-pzps1-realtime/adb-pzps1-realtime-web, update the tag in .do/app.yaml, then run doctl apps update 21dff533-6337-4ca7-8cd6-573efc44b2c3 --spec .do/app.yaml.

checks.description: The app is served over HTTPS with a valid certificate
The app is public: no redirect to another host such as a login page
GET / serves the chat UI as HTML
deployment.json declares a supported transport (websocket or sse)
A message reaches another client in the same room within 5 s
The sender receives its own message too
Messages never reach clients in other rooms
Five users posting at the same time all see every message within 10 s
The chat UI loads in a browser without errors
